title: Job 29
paragraphs: ¹ Job continued speaking. ² "How I long for the months gone by, for the days when God watched over me — ³ when his lamp shone above my head, and by his light I walked through darkness. ⁴ Those were the days of my prime, when God's friendship rested on my house, ⁵ when the Almighty was still with me and my children were all around me.

⁶ When my path ran thick with cream and the rock poured out rivers of olive oil. ⁷ When I walked out to the city gate and took my seat in the public square, ⁸ the young men saw me and stepped aside, and the elders rose to their feet. ⁹ The princes stopped talking and covered their mouths; ¹⁰ the voices of the nobles fell silent and their tongues stuck to the roof of their mouths.

¹¹ Every ear that heard me praised me, and every eye that saw me gave witness in my favor. ¹² For I rescued the poor who cried out, and the fatherless who had no one to help. ¹³ The dying blessed me; I made the widow's heart sing for joy. ¹⁴ I put on righteousness like a garment, and it clothed me; justice was my robe and my crown. ¹⁵ I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.

¹⁶ I was a father to the poor; I took up the case of the stranger I did not know. ¹⁷ I broke the fangs of the wicked and snatched the prey from their teeth. ¹⁸ I thought, 'I will die in my own house, my days as many as the grains of sand.' ¹⁹ My roots reached down to the water; the dew lay fresh on my branches all night. ²⁰ My glory was new in me, and the bow in my hand was always strong.

²¹ Men listened to me and waited; they held their silence at my counsel. ²² After I spoke they did not speak again; my words fell upon them like gentle rain. ²³ They waited for me as for rain, and opened their mouths as if drinking in the spring showers. ²⁴ If I smiled at them, they could hardly believe it; the light of my face was precious to them. ²⁵ I set their course and sat at their head; I lived among them like a king among his army, like one who comforts the grieving.
